Moosend ended its "Free Forever" plan. One commenter said the post announcing it was published on Jan 21 for a shutdown that happened on Jan 20, calling the lack of notice "pretty brutal."

A small SaaS operator said Moosend played a semantic game: it didn't make the plan paid, it terminated free accounts, so "forever" meant only as long as free accounts existed. He called the use of "forever" entirely misleading and said Moosend is now on record as a company that doesn't keep its promises.
On Moosend's replacement for the free plan, a commenter wrote: "free 30 day no obligation trial"... of their most expensive plan. Also known as "exactly what everyone else offers".
A commenter said they didn't fault Moosend for needing to make money, but called the end of the Free Forever plan a great lesson in how not to market a new product.
A commenter compared Moosend dropping its free plan to Google retiring legacy G Suite accounts, asking whether 2022 is "the year of the rugpull."
